text:
sam: FYI reproduced a dangerous window where compaction hard-deletes a prefix while its lease migrates. Putting notes here so we pick a pragmatic short-term fix + followups.

raj: can you drop the minimal log + what node ran compactor vs owner?

sam: logs below, owner moved from node-A -> node-C, compactor on node-A ran shortly after it lost leadership but before it saw the epoch bump.
```
[2026-03-20T03:11:01Z] lease: owner_change tenant=acct:9001 from=node-A epoch=77 -> 78
[2026-03-20T03:11:02Z] compactor(node-A): start compact prefix=acct:9001 epoch_seen=77 compact_trigger=78
[2026-03-20T03:11:02Z] compactor(node-A): hard_delete prefix=acct:9001 bytes=12KB reason=age
[2026-03-20T03:11:03Z] request(node-C): miss; remote_fetch succeeded; inconsistency detected
```

ana: that's scary because clients experienced 50-200ms extra tail as we rehydrated. Not a full outage but data churn and ops noise.

mike: root cause: compactor trusts local epoch snapshot for delete decisions. lease handoff can happen concurrently so snapshot can be stale mid-operation.

raj: brainstormed mitigations:
- compact-safe-window: do not hard-delete prefixes with lease activity in the last X ms (simple guard)
- soft-marker flow: mark prefix "candidate-for-delete" then double-check owner epoch before final GC (two-step)
- live-validate-RPC: on delete, call control-plane OwnerService.validateEpoch(prefix, epoch) sync; if mismatched abort
- auto-tombstone-on-miss: if a fetch after delete reveals inconsistency, create a tombstone and alert, so we don't leave persistent data loss (fast recovery path)

sam: tradeoffs quick take:
- safe-window: easiest rollout, increases on-disk transient retention; must be adaptive to cluster telemetry or will either over-retain or still miss races
- two-step mark->delete: correct-by-design but requires durable marker state + mark-GC backgroundizer + more invariants/tests
- RPC validate: pretty low-friction; cost is an additional RPC on hot path for deletes (rare); good compromise for targeted hosts
- tombstone-on-miss: recovery-focused; still means we briefly lose in-memory cache entries and will do heavier rehydrate write ops

mike: for immediate mitigation propose 2-part hotfix: (1) abort hard_delete if last_lease_transition_ts < safe_window_ms (default 1500ms) (2) make hard_delete do an optional control-plane epoch-validate RPC when flag enabled (opt-in per host).

ana: 1500ms is closer to median in telemetry but as lisa said earlier, must be adaptive. We should also add a metric `compact_hard_delete_aborted_by_safety` and `compact_delete_rpc_latency`.

raj: also add system-pressure escape hatch: if disk_pressure == CRITICAL, allow bypass for LOW_PRIORITY prefixes but never bypass for pinned/high-priority tenants.

sam: agree. Concrete rollout plan:
- hotfix branch implementing safe_window + optional epoch-validate RPC + metrics (PR today).
- canary in staging + 10% prod hosts in us-west (monitor aborted_delete and tombstone creation).
- if false positives high, tune safe_window via pct99 lease-propagation telemetry.

mike: followups RFCs:
- RFC A: Two-phase delete protocol (marker + finalizer) with invariants, failure modes, and GC timeline. high complexity but long-term correct. (owner: raj, ETA 7 days)
- RFC B: Adaptive safe-window algorithm using telemetry histograms and per-cluster configs; include pressure-circuit override rules (owner: ana, ETA 1 week)
- RFC C: Lightweight owner-validate-RPC design + perf budget; propose batch validation endpoint to amortize deletes (owner: mike, ETA 5 days)

ana: tests: need unit + integration: simulate weird timing where leader flips mid-compact, ensure either compactor aborts or archive/tombstone is written and rehydrate path handles it without silent data loss. Also add chaos test that injects high disk pressure while safety window active.

sam: I'll own the hotfix PR (ETA 24h). Raj can start the two-phase RFC draft. Mike will prototype owner-validate RPC and perf harness. Ana will instrument telemetry for lease-propagation percentiles.

ops-bot: deploy-note: hotfix rollout should include kill-switch flag. Canary duration 2 hours, rollback threshold: >5 rehydrates/min for a host.

raj: tiny micro-idea: when marking candidate-for-delete, append current owner-id into marker so finalizer can cheaply verify local ownership without external RPC (if finalizer runs on same owner). But marker must be durable across restarts. Will add to RFC.

mike: remember to update docs for prefix-priority config and compactor tuning in ops playbook.

sam: ok closing thread. I'll paste PR link here when opened and tag reviewers. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
